Abney announces conservation, recreation funding in southwestern Pa.
Rep. Aerion Andrew Abney
October 7, 2026 | 3:48 PM
HARRISBURG, Oct. 7 –
State Rep. Aerion Abney, chair of the Allegheny and Southwest House Democratic Delegation, announced today that four projects across Allegheny County and southwestern Pennsylvania have been awarded funding through Pennsylvania’s Community Conservation Partnerships Program.
The grants support projects focused on workforce development, urban forestry, parks and riverfront planning, as well as conservation efforts across western Pennsylvania.
The grants include:
Pittsburgh Conservation Corps
— funding for workforce development and wood reuse in Allegheny County.
Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy
— funding to support work at Emerald View Park.
Riverlife
— funding for a study of Pittsburgh’s riverfront amenities.
Western Pennsylvania Conservancy
— funding for urban and community forestry efforts throughout Pittsburgh and Western Pennsylvania, including Allegheny, Armstrong, Beaver, Bedford, Blair, Butler, Cambria, Centre, Clarion, Clearfield, Erie, Fayette, Greene, Huntingdon, Indiana, Somerset, Washington and Westmoreland counties.
“These grants will help make southwestern Pennsylvania a stronger, more vibrant place to live,” Abney said. “They support good jobs, improve public spaces and parks and help us make better use of the natural assets that define our region. That’s an investment residents will be able to see and experience for years to come.”
The Community Conservation Partnerships Program, administered by the Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, supports recreation, natural-resource conservation and community revitalization projects across the commonwealth. The program funds a range of efforts, including parks, trails, rivers, open space and community forestry.
“From Pittsburgh’s riverfronts and parks to communities across southwestern Pennsylvania, these projects touch some of the places and priorities that matter most to our region,” Abney said. “I’m proud to see state funding supporting projects that create opportunities, improve quality of life and help position our communities for the future.”

Abney bill to help child welfare providers manage insurance costs passes House
Rep. Aerion Andrew Abney
September 29, 2026 | 4:15 PM
HARRISBURG, Sept. 29 –
The Pennsylvania House of Representatives today passed legislation sponsored by state Rep. Aerion Abney that would help child welfare providers manage insurance costs so they can afford to continue their important work.
A licensed social worker, Abney said
H.B. 2490
will help child welfare providers maintain affordable insurance coverage and serve children, families and communities across Pennsylvania.
“Child welfare providers are facing a serious insurance crisis, with premiums rising sharply and some providers struggling to find coverage at all,” Abney said. “We need to make sure the people and organizations caring for our children can focus on that work instead of being pushed out by insurance costs. This legislation creates a fairer approach to liability and helps protect the stability of these essential services.”
Under the bill, counties would not be allowed to require a child welfare provider to waive an insurer’s right to recover money from a party responsible for a claim as a condition of receiving a county contract.
The legislation addresses a growing problem for providers. Rising insurance premiums and limited coverage options can make it more difficult for organizations to provide child welfare services.
Preventing contract requirements that further increase insurers’ risk can help create greater stability for providers and the children and families who depend on them.
“Pennsylvania’s child welfare system depends on strong providers that can stay open, hire qualified staff and serve families safely,” Abney said. “This bill is about making sure these organizations have the stability they need to continue doing this critical work.”
The bill now heads to the Pennsylvania Senate for further consideration.
Abney represents the 19th Legislative District, which includes Pittsburgh’s Hill District, North Side, South Side, Allentown, Hazelwood, Downtown, The Bluff, Knoxville, Beltzhoover, Manchester, Windgap, Chartiers, Sheraden, Elliott, and North, South and West Oakland neighborhoods.

Abney announces state investments for Pittsburgh communities
Rep. Aerion Andrew Abney
September 15, 2026 | 10:52 AM
PITTSBURGH, Sept. 15 –
State Rep. Aerion Abney today announced more than $3.5 million in Local Share Account funding for Pittsburgh-area projects that will expand access to essential services, strengthen neighborhood infrastructure, preserve historic community assets and improve public spaces.
The announcement also includes a city of Pittsburgh Bureau of Fire engine investment secured by the full Pittsburgh Delegation and a Pittsburgh Land Bank award that Abney secured in partnership with state Rep. Jessica Benham.
"These investments deliver real, lasting improvements for residents throughout Pittsburgh," Abney said. "From bringing library services directly to older adults and ensuring emergency power for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, to creating childcare, expanding educational resources, improving accessibility and revitalizing neighborhood landmarks, these grants meet practical needs while helping our communities grow stronger."
The grants include:
$338,071 for the Allegheny County Library Association's new bookmobile.
This funding will replace the association's nearly 15-year-old bookmobile, helping it continue bringing books, materials, and library services directly to people who may not be able to visit a library branch.
$150,000 for a backup generator at the Center for Hearing & Deaf Services.
The grant will help the center install a commercial backup generator at its Fifth Avenue building.
$400,000 for the Perry Hilltop Citizens Council's 2610 Perrysville Project.
This investment will help turn a long-vacant former American Legion Lodge into a licensed childcare and community event center. The project will preserve an important neighborhood building, create a space for families and community gatherings, and bring new activity to the Perrysville Avenue corridor.
$200,000 for accessible public restrooms at Allegheny Landing.
Riverlife will use this funding to build a permanent, ADA-accessible restroom facility along the Three Rivers Heritage Trail at Allegheny Landing Park. With more than 1.3 million visits to the trail each year, this project will give walkers, cyclists, families, and visitors access to a basic amenity that supports a more welcoming and usable riverfront.
$550,000 for The Education Partnership's warehouse expansion.
The Education Partnership supplies teachers and students throughout southwestern Pennsylvania with the materials they need to learn and succeed. This grant will help the organization build a larger warehouse so it can accept more donations and distribute more school supplies to classrooms across the region, where one in three students lacks essential supplies.
$500,000 for an ADA-compliant elevator at the Neighborhood Resilience Project.
The Neighborhood Resilience Project is expanding its Hill District facility at 2038 Bedford Ave. This funding will help install an elevator so that people with disabilities, seniors, and families can fully access the organization's trauma-informed services and programs on every floor of the building.
$207,544 for the second phase of the Historic Tito House redevelopment.
The funding will help Uptown Partners of Pittsburgh move forward with foundation work, waterproofing, site preparation, and structural construction at the historic Tito House. Saving the building will preserve a distinctive part of Uptown's history, address blight, and help create new opportunities for the neighborhood.
$800,000 for a city of Pittsburgh Bureau of Fire engine.
This investment will help Pittsburgh firefighters continue responding to emergencies with the equipment they need to protect residents, businesses, and neighborhoods.
$450,000 for the Pittsburgh Land Bank.
This funding will help the Land Bank continue its work to move vacant, abandoned, and tax-delinquent properties back into productive use, creating opportunities for housing, redevelopment, and stronger neighborhoods.
"These organizations and public partners know their neighborhoods and the people they serve," Abney said. "I am proud to support their work, and I am grateful to my colleagues in the Pittsburgh Delegation for working together to direct state resources toward projects that make Pittsburgh more inclusive, resilient, and vibrant."

Abney announces cultural and historical grants supporting Allegheny County institutions
Rep. Aerion Andrew Abney
September 10, 2026 | 2:38 PM
PITTSBURGH, Sept. 10 –
State Rep. Aerion Abney today announced more than $200,000 in Pennsylvania Historical & Museum Commission Cultural and Historical Support Grants for four Allegheny County institutions that preserve history, inspire young people, and strengthen communities across the region.
The grants provide essential operating support to the Kamin Science Center, Children’s Museum of Pittsburgh, Senator John Heinz History Center and Holocaust Center of Pittsburgh. Together, the institutions play a vital role in educating students and families, preserving Western Pennsylvania’s history, promoting STEM learning and combating antisemitism and other forms of hate.
“These institutions are a tremendous asset to our community, and I’m proud to see state funding helping them continue their important work,” Abney said. “Whether it’s inspiring a child to pursue a career in science, introducing families to the rich history of our region, or teaching future generations the lessons of the Holocaust, these organizations make a lasting difference in the lives of people throughout Western Pennsylvania.”
The funding is part of nearly $4 million in Cultural and Historical Support Grants announced by the PHMC for the 2026-27 grant cycle. The program provides unrestricted operating support to eligible museums and official county historical societies across Pennsylvania. This year, 182 institutions in 60 counties received grants.
According to the PHMC, the program is designed to strengthen Pennsylvania’s museum and historical community as the Commonwealth continues to preserve and celebrate its history ahead of the nation’s 250th anniversary and beyond.
The institutions receiving grants include:
Kamin Science Center — $47,000: The grant will support operating expenses at the nationally recognized science center, whose interactive exhibits, immersive experiences, planetarium shows and STEM education programs serve students and families throughout the Pittsburgh region and beyond.
Children’s Museum of Pittsburgh — $45,000: Funding will help offset the costs of building and grounds maintenance, utilities, marketing, personnel and insurance as the museum prepares to welcome more than 300,000 children, youth and families in fiscal year 2027. The museum provides hands-on cultural and educational experiences through its Children's Museum, MuseumLab and Buhl Community Park.
Holocaust Center of Pittsburgh, a program of The Tree of Life — $65,000: Funding will support staff salaries associated with preserving and interpreting the Holocaust Center’s permanent collection, operating its public exhibit and providing educational programs connecting Holocaust history to antisemitism and other forms of hate.
The Senator John Heinz History Center, which is located outside Abney’s legislative district, also received a $65,000 Cultural and Historical Support Grant. The grant was supported by members of the Allegheny County legislative delegation, reflecting a broader regional commitment to the History Center and its role in preserving and sharing Western Pennsylvania’s history.
The History Center will use the funding to help launch a major exhibition on the region’s iconic amusement park history, drawing on its extensive Kennywood collection. The funds will also support public programs, publications and operations during the institution’s major facility expansion in Pittsburgh.
“Museums and historical organizations are an important part of what makes Allegheny County such a vibrant place to live, learn and visit,” Abney said. “I’m pleased to join my colleagues across the Allegheny County delegation in supporting these institutions and the work they do for our communities.”
The PHMC grant program is designed to provide unrestricted operating support to qualifying institutions and strengthen Pennsylvania’s museum and historical community as the Commonwealth continues to preserve and celebrate its history in honor of the nation’s 250th anniversary and beyond.
“This funding recognizes that preserving our past and investing in education are investments in our future,” Abney said. “I will continue working with my colleagues to make sure Allegheny County’s cultural and educational institutions have the resources they need to serve residents and visitors for years to come.”

Abney welcomes additional state funding for Pittsburgh transportation improvements
Rep. Aerion Andrew Abney
August 18, 2026 | 9:26 AM
PITTSBURGH, Aug. 18 –
State Rep. Aerion Abney today announced that Pittsburgh has been awarded nearly $3.75 million in state funding through Pennsylvania’s Multimodal Transportation Fund to support two important transportation infrastructure projects in the city.
The awards include $3 million for the renovation of the Boulevard of the Allies in Pittsburgh’s Central Business District and $739,007 to upgrade and expand the North Shore’s overhead lane use control system.
“These investments are about making Pittsburgh’s infrastructure safer, more reliable and better equipped to serve our growing city,” Abney said. “From improving one of our most important downtown corridors to modernizing a critical traffic management system on the North Shore, these projects will make a real difference for residents, workers, businesses and visitors. I’m proud to see state resources coming back to Pittsburgh to strengthen our transportation network and support our local economy.”
The Boulevard of the Allies project will repave the roadway between Commonwealth and Grant streets in Pittsburgh’s Central Business District and add new median planters. The improvements will help make this important downtown corridor safer, smoother and more inviting.
The North Shore Overhead Lane Use Control Upgrade and Expansion project will modernize the overhead lane control system on Pittsburgh’s North Shore. The system is more than 25 years old, and these upgrades will help keep it working safely and reliably for years to come.
The projects are part of a statewide investment of $54 million for 50 highway, bridge, aviation, port, bicycle and pedestrian projects across 27 counties through the Multimodal Transportation Fund. The program is designed to improve safety, strengthen local economies and enhance mobility by investing in transportation infrastructure that connects communities and people to opportunity.
“Transportation infrastructure is foundational to a thriving Pittsburgh,” Abney said. “These grants demonstrate what we can accomplish when state and local government work together to address infrastructure needs and make strategic investments in our communities. I thank the Shapiro Administration and PennDOT for recognizing the importance of these projects and investing in Pittsburgh.”
Abney represents the 19th Legislative District, comprised of the Hill District, North Side, South Side, Allentown, Hazelwood, Downtown, The Bluff, Knoxville, Beltzhoover, Manchester, Allentown, Windgap, Chartiers, Sheraden, Elliot, and North, South and West Oakland sections of Pittsburgh.

Abney

House Democratic Allegheny County Delegation

The Greenlight-Go Program
is a competitive state grant program designed to improve the efficiency and operation of existing traffic signals in Pennsylvania and is administered by the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation.

Capturing and directing new revenue streams can help us strengthen human services, support vulnerable residents, and address critical needs in our communities.
“The court’s four-month stay provides the legislature with an important window to act thoughtfully and responsibly. We should use this opportunity to create a system that promotes fairness, accountability and meaningful public benefit while protecting the organizations that serve as anchors in communities across the Commonwealth.”

First-ever digital advertising tax in PA passes state House
Sponsors Fiedler, Abney, Inglis highlight millions in potential revenue
Rep. Aerion Andrew Abney
June 9, 2026 | 4:31 PM
HARRISBURG, June 9
– Today, the PA House of Representatives passed the "Digital Ads Tax Bill" (
H.B. 1678
) with a bipartisan vote of 139-63. Introduced by state Reps.
Elizabeth Fiedler
, D-Phila.;
Aerion Abney
, D-Allegheny; and
John Inglis
, D-Allegheny, the legislation would update Pennsylvania’s existing gross receipts tax to include the sale of digital advertisements.
The vast majority of the tax would be paid by the wealthiest Big Tech corporations, including Google, Meta, Amazon, TikTok, and Microsoft, which represent an almost
$300 billion
industry in the U.S. The legislation would require multinational corporations to pay their fair share without raising taxes on consumers or small businesses. The tax applies to the platform selling ad space on websites and apps, not the retailer paying to promote their product.
“Plain and simple, this legislation is about requiring big out-of-state corporations profiting off the people of Pennsylvania to pay their fair share in taxes, and to invest in the public services and programs we all count on,” said
Fiedler
, who is the prime sponsor of the bill. “Working people are struggling to pay their bills and are tired of hearing there is no money for their schools, healthcare and transportation. If multinational corporations making record-breaking profits want to do business in our state, then they should pay their fair share just like working people and small businesses do.”
The legislation could have a significant impact on the state’s budget. The bill is designed to close the loophole that has allowed this tremendous profit to escape taxation for years. Updating the gross receipts tax to include digital advertising could raise $500 million annually in new revenue for the state. This revenue is likely to grow, with the digital ads industry projected to be worth $1 trillion in just five years.
“Every day, Pennsylvanians are exposed to digital advertisements that generate billions in profits for some of the world's largest corporations, yet those companies contribute little to nothing in Pennsylvania taxes on that revenue,” said
Abney
. “I am proud to support this legislation because Pennsylvania families and local businesses should not be left carrying the load while multinational corporations profit from our communities without giving back.”
“The Digital Advertising Tax ensures corporations and billionaires are paying more of a fair share of taxes, and it’s about time,” said
Inglis
. “There is still work to be done regarding fair taxes on the wealthy, but this is an exciting and overdue step in the right direction.”
According to a recent report by the Internet Advertising Bureau and PricewaterhouseCoopers, the digital advertising industry saw an
almost 14%
year-over-year increase in 2025. Alphabet (Google) and Meta are currently the
two highest revenue earners
from digital advertising, each reporting over $230 billion in revenue this year.
“These are the biggest, most profitable companies that are bringing data centers and all of the challenges to our commonwealth. 100% they should pay their fair share,” said House Majority Leader
Matt Bradford
, D-Montgomery.
Pennsylvania has one of the most regressive tax structures in the nation, with its poorest residents paying nearly double the tax rate of the wealthiest.
“The gross receipts tax dates back to the 1860s, and our Tax Code was codified in 1971. Who in 1971 anticipated that we’d all be carrying mobile phones in our pockets, watching Smart TVs, and getting ads on these and our computers all day long?” said House Finance Committee Chair
Steve Samuelson
, D-Northampton. “There’s a new report since our hearing on this bill, which shows that in 2025, digital ad revenue rose by 13.9%. This most recent report says that digital ad revenue is $294 billion nationwide. More than $11 billion of this revenue is derived from ads targeting Pennsylvanians.”
House Bill 1678 has
59 co-sponsors
from across the Commonwealth. State Sens.
Lindsey Williams
, D-Allegheny;
Nikil Saval
, D-Phila.; and
Katie Muth
, D-Berks/Chester/Montgomery, have introduced
companion legislation
in the state Senate.  The bill is part of the
“Tax Billionaires. Fund PA”
package.
The House bill now moves to the state Senate for further consideration.

April 15, 2026 | 11:31 AM
PITTSBURGH, April 15
– Today, State Rep. Aerion Abney announced a massive investment from the Pennsylvania Infrastructure Investment Authority to a Pittsburgh Water and Sewer Authority project.
A Pennvest loan of $53,895,600 will go to the authority for sewer rehabilitation in the Hazelwood, Bon Air, Stanton Heights, Overbrook, Chateau, Swisshelm Park, Carrick and Allegheny West areas of Pittsburgh.
The rehabilitation will be done in a proactive manner to avoid the issue and cost associated with full failure of infrastructure. All rehabilitation done will have a new design life of 50 years when completed.
Pennvest’s low-interest loan funding will provide the grant-equivalent of $16,202,005 over the life of the loan. Without the loan, user sewage fees would be expected to increase by 70% to accommodate the project.
“This Pennvest loan will provide crucial sewer rehabilitation and make sure our systems continue to run smoothly for decades to come,” Abney said. “I’m excited that the state has put its might behind these needed renovations, all while keeping fees down for constituents that have affordability on their minds.”

Abney supports new recommendations for storm response
PUC review identifies 10 recommendations for improving responses
Rep. Aerion Andrew Abney
January 6, 2026 | 9:24 AM
HARRISBURG, Jan. 6 —
State Rep. Aerion Abney, D-Allegheny, today expressed his support for a series of new recommendations from the state Public Utility Commission aimed at strengthening storm planning and coordination across Pennsylvania.
The PUC released a
full post-storm review
after spring storms last year battered western Pennsylvania, cutting electric service across swaths of the region and damaging many properties.
The PUC’s analysis resulted in 10 recommendations aimed at improving how utilities prepare for, respond to, and recover from widespread service outages.
“The state has a responsibility to do everything in its power to minimize the effects of severe storms on Pennsylvanians,” Abney said. “There are several ways we can do that, and I’m glad to see the PUC offer concrete recommendations to help protect people across the commonwealth.”
Key recommendations include re-establishing a statewide Electric Distribution Co. Storm Best Practices Group to translate lessons learned from storm responses into measurable improvements. Additional recommendations call on utilities to refine forecasting, strengthen call center performance during high-volume periods, enhance coordination with emergency management agencies, and continue investing in critical infrastructure improvements.
Abney is also sponsoring legislation that would protect Pennsylvanians from price gouging in the aftermath of damaging storms. He introduced the bill after residents reported unusually high repair estimates for storm-damaged properties last spring.
House Bill 1496
would close a critical loophole in the Pennsylvania Price Gouging Act to extend the law’s provisions to local disaster emergencies—those declared by municipalities, counties, or other local governing bodies. Provisions of the current act only apply to price increases during a state of disaster declared by the governor.
The bill cleared the House Consumer Protection, Technology and Utilities Committee in September, and Abney vowed to push for passage by the full House this year.

Allegheny County receives $7.3 million to aid crime victims and community safety
Rep. Aerion Andrew Abney
December 12, 2025 | 9:30 AM
HARRISBURG, Dec. 12 —
The Allegheny County Democratic House Delegation announced today that Allegheny County is receiving $7.3 million in grants to support various programs aiding crime victims and community safety.
The funding comes from the Pennsylvania Commission on Crime and Delinquency.
“These grants will aid our county and justice system in numerous ways—from helping victims navigate the courts to treating addictions to preventing child abuse,” said state Rep. Aerion Abney, chair of the delegation. “On behalf of our Allegheny County Democratic House Delegation, I’m grateful to PCCD for the work they do to ensure this critical funding comes to our county.”
The following grants were awarded to organizations in Allegheny County:
$500,000 to Allegheny-Singer Research Institute
for a program for post-incarcerated patients with a stimulant-use disorder.
$487,424 to Institute for Research, Education and Training in Addiction
for an initiative for treatment placement.
$500,000 to Passages to Recovery Inc.
for peer-advocacy support.
$500,000 to Unity Recovery
for peer-led re-entry support.
$50,000 to A Child’s Place
for citizens advisory and police liaison services.
$49,757 to UPMC-Children’s Hospital
for a public campaign on child abuse prevention.
$53,139 to Women’s Center & Shelter of Greater Pittsburg
for victims’ rights programs and services.
$80,392 to Pittsburgh Action Against Rape
for victims’ rights programs and services.
$855,545 to Center for Victims
for programs and services.
$18,580 to Crisis Center North
for victims’ rights programs and services.
$15,162 to Alle-Kiski Area Hope Center
for victims’ rights programs and services.
$944,851 to University of Pittsburgh
for a program for youth and young adults impacted by community violence.
$200,000 to Allegheny County Chief Executive Officer
for programs to treat opioid-use disorder.
$1.4 million to Allegheny County
for adult probation monitoring and supervision.
$1.5 million to Allegheny County
for adult probation and parole programs.
$148,680 to Scott Township
for a police social worker position.
More information about PCCD funding can be found here:
https://www.pa.gov/agencies/pccd
.

Abney: $920,000 in grants awarded to Pittsburgh projects
Rep. Aerion Andrew Abney
November 18, 2025 | 11:12 AM
HARRISBURG, Nov. 18 —
State Rep. Aerion Abney, D-Allegheny, announced that the
Commonwealth Financing Authority
awarded $920,000 today to invest in projects that will benefit Pittsburgh’s economy.
Grants from the
Gaming Economic Development Tourism Fund
will fund 11 projects in Abney’s district:
$100,000 to the Pittsburgh Opera for operating expenses.
$200,000 to Humane Animal Rescue for HVAC replacements.
$40,000 to Northside Partnership Project for asbestos remediation.
$30,000 to Community of Change Center for renovations and a computer lab.
$75,000 to Citrone Foundation Inc., for a vehicle.
$100,000 to Charles Street Area Corp. for site development.
$50,000 to LEVEL: Equity Building for property acquisition.
$100,000 to BPOE Elks Lodge #33 for rehabilitation work.
$50,000 to City of Pittsburgh for building renovations at Warrington Recreation Center.
$75,000 to Pittsburgh Trust for Cultural Resources for bandshell construction.
$100,000 to Beltzhoover Consensus Group for home construction.
“These are worthwhile projects that will benefit Pittsburgh in many different ways – from housing opportunities to community services to recreation and the arts,” Abney said. “These are the kinds of investments that will ensure that Pittsburgh remains a great place to live and work.”
Established in 2004 by the
Pennsylvania Race Horse Development and Gaming Act
, the GEDTF appropriates funds from gaming revenue to invest in economic development.
